newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines bars East Timorese travellers - report.
newsitem.headline: Philippines bars East Timorese travellers - report.

text.p: Philippine immigration officials have barred the entry of some 100 East Timorese on suspicion they plan to hold protests in Manila next month to demand Indonesia leave East Timor, newspapers said on Saturday.

Indonesian President Suharto is among the world leaders expected to attend a summit conference of 18 member economies of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in Subic Bay near Manila on November 25.

Immigration intelligence chief Orlando Dizon denied entry to the East Timorese when they arrived at the Manila airport on Tuesday on fears they planned to disrupt the APEC summit, Manila newspapers said.
"We (could) have granted them entry, but we were suspicious of their motives," the Philippine Daily Inquirer quoted Dizon as saying.
Immigration officials were out for the weekend and could not be contacted for comment.
The newspapers said the East Timorese told immigration officials they were bound for South Korea to look for employment and were just stopping over in Manila.
East Timorese dissidents are demanding Indonesia's withdrawal from the former Portugese colony.
Indonesia invaded the region in December 1975 and annexed it the following year. The United Nations does not recognize Indonesian rule in East Timor.
East Timor Bishop Carlos Belo and resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta were awarded the 1996 Nobel Peace Price on Friday in a decision that angered Indonesia but won global praise.

Human rights activists condemned Indonesian rule in East Timor in an international conference in Manila in 1994. Several East Timorese tried to attend the meeting but were denied entry by the Philippine government.
